palette.notes: Overworld rooms use very few flat colours per area: the Ruins seen in the clips are pink-magenta floor, darker purple walls, a pale-blue water channel and a brown bridge. Battles are white line art on black with orange menu buttons. No metrics file.

lighting: None to speak of: flat fills, no light direction, no cast shadows. Areas read by their colour, and battles by black emptiness around white shapes.
silhouette: The child is a tiny, simple sprite (striped shirt, brown hair) dwarfed by the room; the battle monster is a big white outline drawing front-on. Simple, iconic shapes that read at small size.

motion.timing: Few frames and long holds; the overworld sprite barely changes while text plays. A single pose or face swap lands a joke (wiki). No frame timings measured.

texture: Flat, clean tiles with a faint repeating floor pattern; low detail keeps focus on text and expression. Critics split on whether it looks amateur; it is a choice.
camera: Top-down rooms with a fixed camera that scrolls with the child; battles cut to a separate black stage with the monster front-on and a small box below.
sound: Each character's speech has its own font and text blip, so voice is designed into the text (wiki).

acting.enters: Characters pop into a room unexpectedly or are revealed by a cut to the black battle screen, then hold a pose while text types out.
acting.acts: Acting through tiny pose and face changes plus typed dialogue; monsters talk mid-fight and their attacks change with how you treat them (wiki).
acting.exits: Characters leave mid-conversation or after a joke, then turn up again later in a new spot.
acting.depth: Mostly flat; recurring characters reappear in later rooms rather than in the background of the same shot.

techniques: one-pose-change punchline with a held beat
character-specific font and text blip as voice
flat colour, no shading, to push expression
few flat colours per area so each place reads instantly
hard cut to a black stage for a confrontation
running character who leaves and pops up again later
feel: flat colour + tiny pose swap + held beat + custom text voice = huge personality from almost nothing
for_fred: Give Fred a running bit: he leaves mid-scene, then pops up later in an unexpected spot holding a new pose. Land jokes with one pose or face swap and a held beat, not a loop. For a confrontation, hard-cut to a black frame with Fred front-on and big.
